inputs.root_cause: SAL-UBL-OBL-788B2748204338B8's (UBL-VALIDATE-001) own missing_behavior said unifying the 5 validation layers into one call 'would additionally require a pluggable business-rule mechanism with a real default rule set... genuinely separate, larger undertaking.' Re-read the rule_text precisely: 'Run syntax, schema, referential, code-list, and pluggable business-rule validation as separately reportable layers' -- 'pluggable' describes an already-required property of the mechanism, and format_factory.ubl.validation.profiles.ProfileValidatorRegistry (UBL-PROFILE-001's own already-implemented, already-tested capability) already IS that pluggable mechanism. The missing_behavior's claim was investigated and found wrong for that half of the compound gap.
inputs.obligation_targeted: 1 obligation narrowed (not closed): SAL-UBL-OBL-788B2748204338B8. The unification half is now resolved; the code-list layer's own automatic document-wide field discovery remains a real, separately-scoped, honestly-documented gap.
inputs.acceptance_evidence: New module validate_all() (validation/combined.py) exercising all 5 layers end-to-end; 11 new tests proving each layer fires independently and in combination, that multiple simultaneous cross-layer violations are all reported together (per the obligation's own 'not stopping at the first error' wording), and that the honestly-scoped code-list layer neither fabricates a pass nor silently skips when a registry IS supplied.
inputs.regression_tier: full ubl package suite plus 6-format regression, mypy --strict, ruff

execution_steps: 1. Re-read the obligation's own precise rule_text (not just its missing_behavior) and checked ProfileValidatorRegistry directly -- confirmed it is a real, frozen, immutable, caller-registerable pluggable validator registry, already fully built for a DIFFERENT obligation (UBL-PROFILE-001) earlier in this project's history, not something needing to be invented.

2. Checked CodeListRegistry.validate_code()'s own signature: operates on one Code value at a time, with no existing document-wide code-field walker (confirmed by grep -- none exists). Decided this piece genuinely remains a separate, larger undertaking (dozens of distinct UBL code-bearing element types would need enumeration), distinct from the unification work itself, and scoped validate_all()'s own code-list layer honestly to caller-supplied codes only rather than fabricating exhaustive coverage.

3. Designed validate_all(source, *, code_registry=None, used_codes=(), profile_registry=None, limits=None) in a new module (validation/combined.py) rather than bloating validator.py: reads raw bytes once (via the same _read_source() load() itself uses, avoiding a double-read on stream sources), attempts loads() for the syntax layer, then runs validate() (chassis/referential via DocumentIndex), schema_validate() (schema layer, gracefully skipped if the optional xmlschema dependency is unavailable), the code-list layer, and validate_profile() (business-rule layer, correctly a no-op when no customization ID matches, per that function's own documented contract) -- collecting every layer's diagnostics into one combined ValidationReport.

4. First end-to-end test run against samples/by-format/ubl/valid/minimal-invoice.xml unexpectedly failed schema validation ('Unexpected child with tag cac:InvoiceLine... Tag cac:LegalMonetaryTotal expected') -- verified independently via schema_validate() directly (not my new code) that this is a real, PRE-EXISTING defect in that specific sample fixture (likely predating FF6-EVENT-000286's own reorder_for_schema_order() fix), unrelated to validate_all() itself. Used a hand-built, schema-conformant Invoice fixture (matching an existing test file's own established _invoice() pattern) for validate_all()'s own tests instead of chasing an unrelated fixture-repair task out of scope for this slice.

5. Found and fixed one real bug in my own first draft: schema_validate() can raise UblParseError (not just SchemaValidationUnavailable) when the raw source can't even be parsed to detect its root element -- added that catch, reporting it as an ubl.schema.unreadable diagnostic rather than letting it propagate.

6. Verified all 5 layers independently: a fully valid document passes with zero diagnostics; malformed XML is caught by the syntax layer; a nonexistent source is caught before any layer runs; an out-of-schema-order element is caught by the schema layer; a duplicate line ID is caught by the referential layer; an out-of-list code is caught by the code-list layer when supplied (and silently skipped, not fabricated, when not supplied); a registered profile validator fires only when its own customization ID matches the document; multiple simultaneous cross-layer violations are all reported together.
7. Exported validate_all from validation/__init__.py and the top-level ubl/__init__.py, alongside the package's other public validation entry points.
8. Wrote 11 tests (test_obligation_unified_validation.py). Ran mypy --strict (clean), ruff (clean), the full ubl suite (1033 passed), and the 6-format regression (3655 -> 3666 passed, +11, 0 failed).

9. Narrowed (not closed) SAL-UBL-OBL-788B2748204338B8 in the ledger: the unification half of its compound missing_behavior is resolved and cited with evidence; the code-list-layer-automatic-discovery half is re-stated precisely and honestly as the one genuinely remaining, separately-scoped gap.
